findings.title: Validation has a side effect that inflates blocked-email match counts
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and saves the record. It runs on every validation pass, not only when a user is actually refused. `valid?` followed by `save`, retries, or any extra validation call will count one blocked attempt several times, so the statistics become unreliable. Read-only checking should be separate from recording a block.

findings.title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive while user emails are normalized
findings.body: `where(email: email)` compares the raw string. User emails are downcased via `Email.downcase` elsewhere, and the uniqueness validation here is also case-sensitive. An entry like `Bad@Spam.com` will not match `bad@spam.com`, so a blocked address can register by changing case. The lookup and storage should normalize the email the same way.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
findings.body: The record is loaded, `match_count` is incremented in Ruby, and the record is saved. Concurrent signups for the same blocked address can lose increments. An atomic `update_counters`/SQL `match_count = match_count + 1` update avoids this.

findings.title: New table added without a corresponding schema.rb update
findings.body: The migration creates `blocked_emails`, but the change set does not touch `db/schema.rb`. Test databases built from schema.rb will not have the table, so `BlockedEmail` specs and any `User` validation that calls `should_block?` will fail with a missing-table error. The schema dump needs to be regenerated and included.

findings.title: Signup failure response exposes blocklist membership to unauthenticated callers
findings.body: The create endpoint is public and now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash`. When an address is blocked, the response carries the distinct `user.email.blocked` message. Anyone can submit arbitrary addresses and learn which ones are on the blocklist. The blocked case should return the same generic message as other email rejections.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is shared across controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the prototype passed to `extend`, so every instance of the controller shares the same array. Rejected emails from one modal session persist into later instances. It should be initialized in `init` or per instance.

findings.title: Domain whitelist/blacklist logic moved here without test coverage
findings.body: The `email_domains_whitelist` and `email_domains_blacklist` checks were moved out of `User` into `EmailValidator`, but the spec only covers the blocked-email path. The moved behaviour, including the new `value =~` usage and `not_allowed` messages, is untested. There is also no test for case-insensitive blocking or for the validator being invoked from `User` validation.

findings.title: should_block? returns nil instead of false when no record exists
findings.body: `record && record.action_type == ...` evaluates to `nil` when no record is found. Callers relying on a boolean will get nil. The spec uses `be_false`, which passes for nil only because of RSpec 2 semantics, so the contract is loose and fragile.
